newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cracks down on drug-money bank accounts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cracks down on drug-money bank accounts.

text.p: U.S. law enforcement agents on Monday froze the assets in about 120 bank accounts suspected of being used to launder profits from drug trafficking, the FBI said.

"We served seizure warrants on about 120 bank accounts today. We believe they are used for money-laundering purposes to repatriate narco-dollars," said Anne Figueiras, spokeswoman for the Federal Bureau of Investigation in Miami.
"We are targeting the accounts, not the account holders. It is an attempt to get back the assets."

The warrants were issued by federal courts and the accounts were frozen as soon as they were served, Figueiras said. She was unable to give a figure for the total sum of assets involved but said, "it's going to be fairly substantial."

A law enforcement source, who asked not be identified, said account holders could be either individuals or companies but as many probably lived outside the United States, they were hard to track down.
"You go for what you can get. If it's the money, get that," the source said.
Figueiras called the crackdown was continuing and more warrants would be served.
The accounts targeted were not only in Miami, which anti-narcotics agents call the command and control centre of Colombian drug trafficking cartels, but also in Texas and New York, she said.
While Colombian cartels are still the main suppliers of illegal narcotics to the United States, Mexican gangs have also been gaining in strength.
"Money has always gone through to Mexico but now its increasingly so," the source said.
He said that once the accounts were frozen it still had to be proven in court that money was acquired or used illegally before it was forfeited.
